title: Sample data: support360_manage_ticket_queue
description:
STOP PATCHING THE ERROR. I need you to diagnose and fix the complete Status/Assign workflow at the source. Do not give me another plan unless you are unable to make a required change.

The issue is STILL NOT RESOLVED.

I have created an actual ticket successfully with:

Ticket: TKT-2026-000456
Initial Status: Open

The ticket already exists in the database.

When I try to Assign this existing Open ticket to an agent, the application blocks the save with:

"A new ticket must be created with status 'Open', not 'Assigned'"

This proves that the current status validation is incorrectly treating an UPDATE of an existing ticket as CREATE/new-record validation.

1. FIND THE REAL ROOT CAUSE

Do NOT simply change the error message or disable the validation.

Trace the complete execution path:

Manage All Tickets → Edit existing ticket → STATUS changed Open → Assigned → validation → save

Identify:

Which model contains the STATUS field.
Which validation is attached to STATUS.
Whether the validation runs during CREATE, UPDATE, or both.
What framework context is available for the existing record.
How the current/previous STATUS is actually supplied to the business logic.
Whether another old validation is also attached to STATUS.
Whether the generated model contains an outdated copy of the validation.
Whether the Assign action itself is invoking the wrong validation.

Do not assume that fixing validate_ticket_status_transition automatically fixes the deployed model. Verify the actual model wiring.

2. CORRECT CREATE BEHAVIOR

For a genuinely NEW ticket:

CREATE

The ticket must start with:

Open

If someone tries to create a new ticket with Assigned, reject it with a normal validation message.

This validation must happen only in the CREATE context.

3. CORRECT UPDATE BEHAVIOR

For an EXISTING ticket, do NOT apply the "new ticket must be Open" rule.

Instead, determine:

previous/existing status → requested/new status

and validate the transition.

The supported workflow is:

Open → Assigned → In Progress → Resolved → Closed

Therefore:

Open → Assigned = VALID
Assigned → In Progress = VALID
In Progress → Resolved = VALID
Resolved → Closed = VALID

Invalid backward/skipped transitions should be rejected with a normal validation message.

4. FIX THE ASSIGN ACTION

When an Admin uses Manage Ticket Queue → Assign:

Admin selects an existing Open ticket.
Admin selects an agent.
Assign action updates the existing ticket.
ASSIGNED_AGENT is populated.
STATUS becomes Assigned.
Assignment is recorded in Activity Log.
No CREATE validation should run.
No "new ticket must be Open" error should appear.
No RuntimeError should occur.

If the Assign action is currently implemented incorrectly, fix the action itself rather than modifying unrelated validation.

5. REMOVE OLD/BROKEN LOGIC

Search the entire Support360 application for all implementations/wiring related to:

Status transition sequence

STATUS_SEQ

validate_ticket_status_transition

SUPPORT360_TICKET

Find duplicate, outdated, or incorrectly attached validations.

There must be one authoritative status-transition implementation.

Make sure the runtime is not still executing an older validation after the new one has been generated.

6. NO RAW SQL

The previous error was:

psycopg2.errors.UndefinedTable: relation "twasta.SUPPORT360_TICKET" does not exist

and later:

SyntaxError: syntax error at or near "SUPPORT360_TICKET"

These errors must NEVER occur again.

Do not use:

UPDATE twasta.SUPPORT360_TICKET

db.t('SUPPORT360_TICKET')

raw SQL strings referencing SUPPORT360_TICKET

or any hardcoded schema-qualified table name.

Use only the platform-supported model/record/database APIs and framework-provided record context.

7. DO NOT DISABLE THE VALIDATION

Do NOT solve this by:

removing the Status validation,
allowing every status,
forcing Status to Open,
bypassing validation,
hardcoding a particular ticket,
or hiding the error.

The actual business workflow must work correctly.

8. CHECK BOTH SCREENS

The same underlying ticket workflow must work consistently in:

Manage All Tickets

and

Manage Ticket Queue

Do not fix one screen while leaving the other screen connected to the old logic.

9. DEPLOY THE ACTUAL FIX

After modifying the logic:

REBUILD → DEPLOY → VERIFY MODEL WIRING → VERIFY BUSINESS LOGIC

Do not tell me "code generation passed" as proof that the issue is fixed.

The fix is NOT complete until the deployed runtime uses the corrected validation.

If a deployment/cache/rebuild step is required, perform it.

If you cannot perform a required step automatically, explicitly tell me the exact designer action I must perform.

10. TEST THE ACTUAL WORKFLOW

Use this acceptance test:

Test 1

Create new ticket
↓
Status = Open
↓
Save successfully

Test 2

Existing Open ticket
↓
Assign agent
↓
Status = Assigned
↓
Save successfully

Test 3

Assigned
↓
Start Progress
↓
In Progress

Test 4

In Progress
↓
Resolve
↓
Resolved

Test 5

Resolved
↓
Confirm Close
↓
Closed

Test 6

Try an invalid transition
↓
It should show a normal validation message
↓
It must NOT show RuntimeError, SQL error, SyntaxError, or SUPPORT360_TICKET does not exist.

11. VERY IMPORTANT

Do not ask me what the problem is. I have already provided the exact symptom, error message, ticket number, affected screen, and expected workflow.

Do not give me another explanation of what you intend to do. Make the changes.

Do not stop after fixing the source file. Verify that the corrected implementation is actually wired to the deployed STATUS validation.

Do not claim "fixed" because a review or generation step passed.

If one tool fails, continue using the available Twasta designer/model/business-logic tools instead of abandoning the fix.

The acceptance criterion is simple: I must be able to take an existing Open ticket and successfully assign it to an agent so that its status becomes Assigned.

Fix the root cause now and deploy the complete correction.
